Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. An economy the IMF expects to grow 8.4 percent in 2026, still priced in large part like the frontier market it stopped being in September.

Latest Report · Tuesday, November 10, 2026

Mispriced Countries: Eight Economies on the Verge

Eight economies on the verge. Index committees and IMF calendars are about to reprice whole markets on dates already printed. The question is which of the world’s cheapest markets are cheap by mistake, and which are cheap because the risk is real.

Eight countries rank, and the ranking is not a list of the cheapest markets in the world. It is a list of markets whose price still belongs to an old label after the label has started to change. Vietnam ranks first and Nigeria second, because their catalysts are dated events on a calendar, an index upgrade phasing in on schedule and a frontier restoration already in effect, and because their multiples stay low even after you charge them honestly for their risk. Egypt is cheaper than both and ranks third, because cheapness alone is not the argument.

Argentina is the warning that runs under the whole report. A market that looked like the great mispricing of the decade reminded everyone in one week in November why it was cheap in the first place. The difference between a mispricing and a market correctly pricing risk is the only thing being judged here, country by country.

The ranking lives in the distance between price and risk. Poland is twice Egypt’s price and carries the lowest bar in the set, a cost of equity of 10.21 percent against Egypt’s 18.82 percent. A low multiple is only cheap if earnings can grow, in dollars, faster than that bar eats them.

Source: MSCI Egypt factsheet, Oct 30, 2026; SSI Research via Vietstock, Nov 9, 2026; MSCI Poland against MSCI All World. Full charts and sourcing inside the report.

Inside the Report
01 The Verdict

The Bottom Line

Vietnam first, Nigeria second, Egypt third, stated plainly before anything else. Argentina is the warning that runs under the whole report.

 8 ranked6 set aside→ 02 The Argument

A Country Gets Refiled Before It Gets Repriced

Index upgrades and IMF programme exits are dated, mechanical events. Money is required to move when they land. Prices, most of the time, move later.

 Sep 2027When the crossings complete→ 03 The Shortlist

Eight Countries, Ranked by the Crossing

The order is the order of confidence in the crossing, not the order of cheapness. Egypt is the cheapest name here and sits third. That inversion is the whole point.

 5.74xCheapest, ranked third→ 04 The Price of Risk

Cheap Is a Price. Mispriced Is a Price Measured Against Risk.

Before any country is praised for being cheap, it gets charged for its risk, in the open, from sourced parts. Poland needs 10.21 percent a year. Egypt needs 18.82 percent.

The Leaders

Vietnam and Nigeria lead the ranking, because their catalysts are dated and their multiples stay low after the risk charge. The rest of the list is measured against them.

Rank 1 · Vietnam

The upgrade is done, the bigger one is next

FTSE began moving Vietnam from frontier to emerging in September 2026, in dated phases that complete in September 2027. Foreigners own just 12.6 percent of the market and have been selling at a record pace.

8.4% IMF growth forecast, 2026
11.7x VN-Index P/E, about 9.0x ex-Vingroup Read the Vietnam section → Rank 2 · Nigeria

Written back into the index

FTSE restored Nigeria from Unclassified to Frontier on September 21, 2026. The naira float held, inflation fell from near 35 percent to about 15 percent, and the banks still trade at half of book value.

THE BOARDPURPOSE

Why The Board exists.

By Josh Pilcher · New reports Tuesday and Friday evenings

I don’t have a ton of time. It’s hard to keep up.

There are so many conflicting narratives, fed by conflicting interests. It feels hard to know what is true, and I know I’m not alone in that.

I often have questions I want answered, or things I don’t understand, that the news simply doesn’t cover. Not all of the time, but sometimes. When that happens, there is nowhere obvious to go for a straight answer.

In my ideal world, I build something useful to me. Something I enjoy reading. Because if I do, so will other people, and it will help them too.

What that looks like in a year, who knows.

From the Latest Report

What to watch next

Ten dated tests that will start settling the argument. The first five:

  1. 1Nov 26 to 30, 2026 · Argentina’s gas decisionThe YPF, Eni and XRG liquefied natural gas final investment decision is targeted for this window. A signature on schedule is the first evidence that the November risk spike was a scare rather than a verdict.
  2. 2Dec 15, 2026 · Egypt stands aloneThe $8 billion IMF programme ends and the final reviews unlock about $2.3 billion. The first debt auctions and the first month of currency trading after that date are the real review.
  3. 3End of Jan 2027 · Vietnam’s spending deadlineAbout VND350 trillion of public investment is due to be disbursed by now. Delivery confirms the growth print behind the upgrade; a slip says the 9 percent quarters were the peak.
  4. 4Q1 2027 · Vietnam’s counterparty testThe central counterparty must be operational for MSCI to move. In March the FTSE phase-in reaches 20 percent, the first dated check on whether foreign selling finally turns.
  5. 5Apr 30 and Jun 30, 2027 · Indonesia’s verdictMSCI’s consultation closes in April and its reclassification decision lands by the end of June. A reprieve reopens a market down by a third; a Standalone ruling confirms the drop.
